title: Jungle rice weed in Paddy Rice

Header: Jungle rice weed in Paddy Rice

Prevention: Purchase certified clean rice seed to avoid introduction through contamination
Clean equipment and farm machinery to prevent seeds being spread
Control established populations near waterways by pulling or hoeing to prevent spread during flooding and storm events
Before planting seed, prepare seed bed and wait for the first rain showers to promote weed germination then control by use of a post-emergent herbicde (glyphosphate) when weeds are 2-3 weeks old
Monitoring: Annual grass, with fibrous, rather shallow roots.
Culms stout, erect with spreading open growth; often branching from base, 20-60cm tall.
Leaves light green, sometimes with tranverse purple bands, inflorescence erect or nodding, 5-15cm long.
No awns gives less spikey appearence than
Jungle rice weed stem has a reddish purple tinge and the rice crop stem is green
Inspect fields every 2 weeks, in particular during and shortly after the wet season, and consider direct control when present
Look out for it in wetlands and along waterways.
Water and storm events can spread seeds
Direct Control: Hand-pull or hoe the weed before flowering
Flood rice fields with 15-22 cm of water, to prevent weeds from developing, until the dough stage.
Flooding with 2-3 cm water will offer limited control
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
Penoxsulam (20 to 180g per litre of active ingredient per hectare)
U (unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use)
Use glyphosate (360g per litre of active ingredient per hectare) before planting rice when there is a heavy infestation.
Butachlor + Propanil (600g per litre of active ingredient per hectare)
